exact_results: The literal polynomial substitutions v=x+i*y, vb=x-i*y and x=(v+vb)/2, y=(-i/2)*(v-vb) are inverses on all complex polynomials in two independent variables. The inverse substitution preserves homogeneous degree.
A homogeneous balanced polynomial in v,vb of degree 2*m is its balanced monomial coefficient times (v*vb)^m. A homogeneous balanced polynomial of degree 2*m+1 vanishes.
The coefficient of x^k*y^0 in c*(x^2+y^2)^m equals c when k=2*m and zero otherwise, with arbitrary natural m,k and complex c.
If P is homogeneous of degree 2*m and so2PolynomialToBalanced(P) has balanced support, P = C(P.coeff(single 0 (2*m)))*(X0^2+X1^2)^m. If the degree is 2*m+1 it is zero.

For every P whose literal transformed polynomial Q=so2PolynomialToBalanced(P) has balanced support, P = sum over m in Q.support.image(d maps to d0) of C(P.coeff(single 0 (2*m)))*(X0^2+X1^2)^m. The index set is a concrete finite set and the coefficients are original Cartesian coefficients.
semantic_checks: The variables v and vb are independent complex polynomial variables. No complex conjugacy relation is imposed in the polynomial ring.
Balance means actual support exponents d0=d1. It is an explicit hypothesis and is not inferred here from the name SO(2) or from a physical symmetry claim.
The first-coordinate exponent map is proved injective on balanced support. Exact coefficient extraction of the finite radial sum therefore has no multiplicity factor or exponential conversion factor.
All original-axis coefficient statements refer to the exponent Finsupp.single 0 (2*m), hence exactly zero y exponent.
Zero polynomial, empty support, degree zero, m=0, and arbitrary coefficients are included. The odd theorem does not require P nonzero.
The finite general result has no homogeneous-degree assumption, degree bound, positivity premise, analytic premise, or numerical approximation.
